meta.source: Coded from the published QP and mark scheme (1MA1_2F_2506). Derived metadata only — question numbers, marks and skill tags. No exam question text transcribed.
meta.note: Marks per part read from the question paper's own part totals and checked against the printed 80. Questions 20 to 27 are the overlap questions shared with 2H (2H q1 to q8) and are tagged identically there.

coding_notes: q1 (weeks to days) tagged time_calculations rather than converting_measurements: the latter is the metric-units node, and nothing metric is involved.

q5 (choose a sensible metric unit for a length and for a mass) tagged converting_measurements. No 'choose an appropriate unit' node exists, but knowing which unit fits a quantity sits squarely inside that skill's territory.

q7 tagged substitution, not solving_linear_equations: the mark scheme rewards a single division by the rate, so claiming the student can solve linear equations would over-credit a one-step reversal of a given rule.
q13a tagged indices rather than simplifying_indices — writing a repeated product in index form is index notation, not the index laws.

q16a (speed from a distance-time graph, answer in a different time unit) tagged kinematic_graphs first so the item files under Algebra with the rest of the graph work, with compound_units second for the unit change.

q22b (effect on the number of bags when each bag covers less) is tagged with its parent question's skill, areas_of_compound_shapes. The mark is for a statement about the consequence rather than for new mathematics, and splitting it into Number would scatter one question across two topic columns.

q24 tagged reverse_percentage although the decrease is given as a fraction: the mark scheme's routes are 'recognise 8000 is four fifths' and 'recognise 8000 is 80%', and reverse_percentage is the taxonomy's only node for working back to an original amount.
